headline: Threat recognition distinguishes real danger from perceived—sorting genuine risks from false alarms
universal_truth: Not everything that feels dangerous is; not everything that is dangerous feels threatening; learn to distinguish
fun_facts: Our threat detection evolved for predators and tribal conflict, not modern risks
Most things that trigger fear responses are not actually dangerous
Real threats are often boring and gradual—like poor diet—not dramatic and sudden
discussion_questions: What feels threatening but isn't actually dangerous?
What's actually dangerous that doesn't trigger your alarm?
How do you calibrate threat detection to reality?

hook.script: Public speaking terrifies people, but it's not dangerous. Meanwhile, sugar quietly damages health without triggering fear. Our threat detection is miscalibrated for modern life. Learning to recognize real threats matters.

cliff.script: Our fear response evolved for different threats than we face today. How do we recognize what's actually dangerous?
cliff.prompt: How do we identify real threats?

options.text: Real threat recognition requires overriding instinct with analysis—our evolved fears don't match modern dangers; we must consciously evaluate what actually causes harm
options.response: Yes. Fear evolved for tigers, not spreadsheets. We fear public speaking but not sedentary lifestyles. Real threat recognition means analyzing actual risk, not just feeling fear.
Gut feelings helped in ancient environments, but modern threats are often invisible to instinct...

fact1.title: Evolved Mismatch
fact1.script: We evolved to fear predators, heights, snakes. We didn't evolve to fear cars, sugar, inactivity. Our threat radar was calibrated for a world that no longer exists.

fact2.title: Boring Dangers
fact2.script: Real dangers are often boring: chronic stress, poor diet, insufficient exercise, financial neglect. They don't trigger alarm because they're gradual and familiar.

fact3.title: False Alarms
fact3.script: Many things that feel dangerous aren't: rejection, public speaking, failure, looking foolish. The fear is real, but the danger isn't. Distinguish feeling from reality.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Not everything that feels dangerous is; not everything that is dangerous feels threatening. Learn to distinguish real threats.

outro.script: That's Day 316. Tomorrow, we'll explore your body's alarm system—instincts and signals. Until then, consider what you fear versus what actually threatens you.

growTrack.title: Threat Calibration - What's Really Dangerous?
growTrack.learning_objective: Distinguish real threats from perceived ones
growTrack.activity: List what you fear. List what actually endangers you (health, finances, relationships). Compare the lists. Where is fear misaligned with threat? Recalibrate your threat detection to reality.
